synopsis: Town boards focused heavily this week on finalizing warrant articles and committee positions ahead of Special Town Meeting. The Advisory Committee voted to recommend $240,000 to connect two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill to municipal water, but finalized unfavorable recommendations for CPA funding toward the Peninsula Trail bridge and golf course irrigation. The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance the Peninsula Trail funding article as originally drafted, while the Trails and Golf committees finalized voter presentation materials. Additionally, the Zoning Board of Appeals voted to support a two-family dwelling zoning article without altering minimum lot language, and the Select Board reviewed initial findings from a town government structure study.

highlights.title: Advisory Committee backs Parkerville landfill water funding
highlights.why: The committee voted 6-0 to recommend Town Meeting approve $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the landfill to municipal water, with the town covering service lines into the houses.

highlights.title: CPC advances Peninsula Trail bridge article without cuts
highlights.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance the $428,550 bridge funding request to Town Meeting as printed, rejecting proposals to remove contingency funding despite cost concerns raised by other boards.

highlights.title: ZBA supports two-family zoning article as drafted
highlights.why: The board voted to present the warrant article to Town Meeting without removing minimum lot requirement language, concluding after legal review that last-minute alterations could create zoning ambiguity.

highlights.title: Advisory Committee opposes CPA funding for golf irrigation
highlights.why: The committee finalized report text opposing the use of Community Preservation Act funds for the roughly $1 million golf irrigation project, maintaining that the course was intended to be self-funding.

highlights.title: Select Board reviews municipal governance structure study
highlights.why: Consultants presented an overview examining town manager authority, bylaws, and Southborough's 68 committees in comparison to other Massachusetts communities.
